title: A harness decides which runtime to invoke, and has no default
query: tools/agent_invocation.py resolves which agent, model, adapter and agent-specific flags a harness will use, and has no default for any of them; an unconfigured invocation refuses rather than guessing. Read it and say why the absence of a default is the correct behaviour for an evaluation harness rather than an inconvenience, and what a results file would have to record for a rate computed from it to be attributable.
oracle: R2: read one file and reason about a design decision, which is analytical rather than a lookup. Inline. The answer is that a silent default measures one vendor and reports the result as a property of the kernel, so refusing is the only option that keeps a number attributable — and that means the results file must carry the resolved agent, model, adapter and flags, because a rate over a mixed pool is a rate over the pool. The trap is calling the missing default a usability gap to be fixed.
